output:
To: group:levy-longsight-noticeboard
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fake blue pills: please read, and please share

Please read this one properly, even if you've already scrolled past the police warning. I'm putting it in its own post so it doesn't get lost in the other thread.

Police have warned that blue tablets are being sold round south Manchester as diazepam or "Xanax". They aren't. Some of them have nitazenes in, which are synthetic opioids and way stronger than heroin. You can't tell by looking. Someone who thinks they're taking something mild could be in serious trouble within a short time.

What to look out for: extreme drowsiness, pinpoint pupils, slow or noisy breathing, blue lips.

If you see that, ring 999 straight away. Not in ten minutes, not after you've tried to wake them. Straight away. The call handler will talk you through what to do until help gets there.

Please hear this next bit. Do not put them to bed to sleep it off. I'm a nurse and this is the thing that worries me most. When mates panic, they put someone on a bed or a sofa, tell themselves they'll be grand in the morning, and ring hours later when it's got worse. By then the brain has been without oxygen too long. Slow or noisy breathing isn't sleep. If you can't wake them properly, it's an emergency.

And please don't let the fear of getting in trouble stop you ringing. The police have said themselves that their priority is preserving life. A mate who's alive and furious with you is a much better outcome than the alternative.

There's also something you can do before anything happens. Naloxone nasal spray reverses the effects of opioids. You can get it free from Brightpath drug and alcohol service on Stockport Road, next to the launderette. Anyone can ask, and you don't have to give your name. The training takes about 10 minutes. They're open Monday to Friday 10 till 4, and Thursdays till 7. It doesn't replace 999, you still ring, but it can buy time.

To the parents: talk to your kids this week. Not after half term, not when there's a good moment, this week. I did it with my lad (he's 14) last night over his tea. Lots of eye rolling. But he listened, and he asked me what pinpoint pupils meant, so it went in. You don't need a big speech. Just tell them these pills are out there, that they can look like something harmless, and that if a friend goes down they ring 999 and stay with them. Tell them they will never be in bother with you for ringing.

To the teenagers who might be reading this: you're not going to get a lecture from me. Just remember that if someone's out of it and you can't wake them, you ring. Even if you're scared, even if it's someone else's house, even if you shouldn't have been there. Ring.

And to anyone tempted to slag the kids off: it helps nobody. Scared kids don't ring for help, and that's the whole problem. If they think they'll be shouted at or punished, they'll hide it, wait, and hope. We want them to pick up the phone straight away, so we need to make that the easy thing to do.

Please share this, don't just like it. Put it on your own page, in the school parents' chat, the football WhatsApp, the family group, anywhere there are parents or teenagers. It only works if it reaches the people who need it.

Thank you. Now I'm off to bed.
